Caveats (cards may carry several), with their direction: does the term allow outcomes the printed card does not (allows more), forbid outcomes it allows (forbids some), or both? A card imported with caveats is in general neither an over- nor an under-approximation of its printed card, so the imported pool must not be used for "no deck can ..." arguments without checking the caveat.

| caveat | direction | cards | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `upTo0` | allows more | 33 | 'up to N' in a Trainer or an Ability allows 0 in the model; the rulebook asks for at least 1 outside attacks (2026 rulebook p. 21; Known gaps, zone moves item) |
| `mayFail` | allows more | 17 | an attach or Bench placement may do nothing in the model (`attach` and `putBench` always allow nothing), a superset of the printed 'attach a …' from the hand or discard pile, and of 'if you can' (Known gaps) |
| `aceSpec` | allows more | 15 | the ACE SPEC deck-building limit is not modelled (no deck construction in the model) |
| `moveMayFail` | allows more | 11 | a move of Energy is `moveEnergy`, which may move nothing (`moveNone`; Known gaps, zone moves item: 'attach, putBench and moveEnergy may always do nothing, a superset of "if you can"'), where print moves one Energy if one can be moved |
| `selfBench` | allows more | 10 | 'this Pokémon' on the Bench is one Benched Pokémon chosen when the effect resolves, and for an on-play Ability the Active Pokémon or a Benched one (Known gaps, Abilities, M8a: `SelfOp`) |
| `moveAnyPair` | allows more | 9 | a move of Energy printed between particular Pokémon ('to this Pokémon', 'from 1 of your Benched Pokémon to your Active Pokémon') is a move between any two of the player's Pokémon (moveEnergy) |
| `searchAny` | allows more | 8 | a deck search for 'a card' (any card) may find nothing in the model, where print must take at least 1 (2026 rulebook p. 21: 'for any effect that allows you to search your deck or discard pile for any card you want and doesn't specify what kind, you must choose at least 1'; Known gaps, zone moves item: 'a superset elsewhere and for an attack that searches for any card') |
| `hiddenInfo` | allows more | 6 | a sentence that only reveals or looks at cards is a no-op (hidden information is not modelled, Known gaps) |
| `trigKO` | allows more | 4 | 'is Knocked Out by damage from an attack' is read as 'Knocked Out by a Knock Out check while the turn's attack has been made': Knock Outs by damage counters the attack placed, by later rounds of the check, and in the check after a failed Confused attempt also fire it (Known gaps, triggered Abilities, M8b) |
| `onePerName` | allows more | 3 | 'You can't use more than 1 X Ability each turn' is not modelled: the use flag is per Pokémon, so each of several Pokémon with that Ability can use it in the same turn |
| `noopUse` | allows more | 2 | an activated Ability whose effect may do nothing in the model in a state where it could do something (as noopPlay) can be used to no effect there, marking its Pokémon as used; the importer reads the ruling of noopPlay for Abilities too, and states the precondition where public information decides it (noop.py; Known gaps, item on plays to no effect) |
| `noopPlay` | allows more | 1 | a Trainer (an Item, a Supporter, a Stadium's use) whose effect may do nothing in the model in a state where it could do something (heal 30 damage from 1 of your Pokémon: the model may heal an undamaged one, as it has no test of a Benched Pokémon's damage) can be played to no effect there. The importer reads the usual ruling, not in the rulebook (2026 p. 12 says only 'When you play any Trainer card, do what it says'): a card may not be played when its effect cannot do anything, except that a search of a hidden zone may find nothing; where public information decides it the term states the precondition instead (noop.py; Known gaps, item on plays to no effect) |
| `oppBenchFresh` | forbids some | 5 | a Basic Pokémon an effect puts onto the opponent's Bench enters play `fresh` and stays so through its owner's next turn, so it cannot evolve then (Known gaps, item on Pokémon put onto the opponent's Bench: whether that turn is its first turn in play is not settled; if it is not, the model forbids an evolution print allows) |
| `anyAmount60` | forbids some | 4 | 'discard any amount / all … for each card you discarded in this way' is `forUpTo` with the bound 60, the cards of a legal deck (2026 rulebook p. 21): exact for every state in which the player has at most 60 cards that could be discarded (`Run.forUpTo_complete`, `discardActive_le`); the model does not require this of a start state, and beyond it a larger discard is forbidden (Known gaps, zone moves item: 'exact for "any amount" once the bound covers the cards that can be taken'); for 'discard all' with more than 60 the attack has no resolution |
| `failToFind` | forbids some | 4 | a mandatory take from a private window ('a Basic Energy card you find there' among the top cards of the player's own deck) is `Qty.most`, which must take a passing card when there is one: fewer outcomes than the usual practice of failing to find in a private window, which the 2026 rulebook does not state (Known gaps, zone moves item, hidden information) |
| `koCheckup` | forbids some | 4 | 'Knocked Out during your opponent's last turn' (any cause) is `Count.koLast w false`, and the model records Knock Outs at Pokémon Checkup in no turn (Known gaps, one-turn history, milestone MV2): a Knock Out by Poison or Burn after the opponent's turn does not make the test true; whether the printed condition counts it was not checked against a ruling |
| `movedUpPromotion` | forbids some | 3 | 'moved from your Bench to the Active Spot this turn' is `InPlay.movedUp`, which a promotion after a Knock Out of the player's own Active Pokémon in their own turn does not set (Known gaps, one-turn history, milestone MV2: an under-model) |
| `trigBenched` | forbids some | 2 | 'Whenever your opponent's Active Pokémon moves to the Bench during their turn' (`TrigEvent.oppBenched`, milestone MV7) resolves when the event happens, before the Knock Outs it causes, on the holders marked at the event: a Pokémon switched in at or above its HP (a static HP change that reads its place or its Energy) gets the effect and is then Knocked Out, and its replacement gets nothing, where under a reading that takes the Knock Out first the effect falls on the replacement; and in a state no play is known to reach (a trigger pending with an Active Spot empty) a marked holder Knocked Out first fires nothing (Known gaps, triggers of the event 'your opponent's Active Pokémon moves to the Bench': the order item and the unreached states) |
| `perPokemon` | both | 83 | a lingering effect printed on one Pokémon ('this Pokémon', 'the Defending Pokémon') is a modifier of its player in the model (Known gaps: modifiers belong to a player) |
| `benchMods` | both | 78 | attack damage to Benched Pokémon takes no bonus, reduction or prevention in the model (Known gaps, milestone M3) |
| `recoil` | both | 69 | self-damage ('also does N damage to itself') is written as damage counters (selfDamage): no Weakness, Resistance or modifier applies to it (Known gaps) |
| `staticBench` | both | 17 | a static damage reduction ('takes N less damage from attacks') is subtracted at step 5 of the damage calculation, which only damage to the Active Pokémon passes through: attack damage to a Benched Pokémon takes no reduction in the model (Known gaps, milestone M3: Bench damage takes no bonus, reduction or prevention; milestone M6) |
| `trigDamaged` | both | 16 | 'is in the Active Spot and is damaged by an attack' is decided on the attack's damage step (HitRun, HitTrig): a Pokémon damaged and then switched to the Bench by the same attack fires nothing, and when the Defending Pokémon was already at or above its HP before the damage step the trigger may fire or not (Known gaps, triggered Abilities, M8b: the two departures, one in each direction) |
| `trigAttacker` | both | 15 | 'the Attacking Pokémon' is the opponent's Active Pokémon when the trigger resolves: if the attack switched its attacker out ('damaged'), or the attacker was Knocked Out by the same check ('Knocked Out'), the effect falls on the new Active Pokémon instead of the attacker or nothing (Known gaps, triggered Abilities, M8b) |
| `ignFxStadium` | both | 12 | 'isn't affected by any effects on your opponent's Active Pokémon' (`Ign.fx`, milestone MV3) switches off step 5 of the damage calculation, which in the model includes the reductions and preventions a Stadium gives the defender (Known gaps, Weakness and Resistance item: `Ign`, step 5); whether the printed text ignores a Stadium's effect was not checked against a ruling |
| `koAttackWide` | both | 8 | 'Knocked Out by damage from an attack during your opponent's last turn' is read as 'Knocked Out by the Knock Out check after the turn's attack' (`Count.koLast w true`): Knock Outs by damage counters an attack's effect placed also count (Known gaps, one-turn history, milestone MV2) |
| `koCounters` | both | 7 | '… is Knocked Out' / 'Knock Out …' is written as 9999 damage counters on that Pokémon (`selfDamage`, `counters`, `benchCounters`, `benchSome`), which the batch Knock Out step takes as a Knock Out with its Prize cards and promotion (Known gaps, self-Knock-Out Abilities; `SelfKO.self_ko`): exact while every derived HP in the game is below 9999 counters (over the imported pool a Pokémon's derived HP is at most 76 + 4E counters, E the Energy cards attached to it, so below in every game of two 60-card decks; the importer checks this bound, survey S11) and nothing prevents damage counters being placed on it (no such effect is modelled); above that the Pokémon survives where print Knocks it Out. A Knock Out written so inside an attack is one by the check after the attack, which the readers of 'Knocked Out by damage from an attack' count (their own caveats trigKO, koAttackWide) |
| `prizes6` | both | 5 | 'Prize cards taken' is `Count.prizesTaken w`, 6 less the Prize cards left (milestone MV4): exact in a game set up with 6 Prize cards (2026 rulebook p. 8), which the model does not require of a start state (Known gaps: setup is not modelled; `Count.prizesTaken`); from another start it is the shortfall from 6, at least 0 |
| `staticPreventBench` | both | 5 | a static prevention ('Prevent all damage done to this Pokémon by attacks from your opponent's F', `SEff.prevent`, milestone MV3) protects the Pokémon only in the Active Spot: attack damage to a Benched Pokémon reads no static effect in the model (Known gaps, milestone M3: Bench damage takes no bonus, reduction or prevention; `GameState.sPrevent` is read at step 5, for the Active Pokémon) |
| `printedRetreat` | both | 4 | 'for each Colorless in your opponent's Active Pokémon's Retreat Cost' is `Count.retreat`, the printed Retreat Cost (milestone MV6): a static effect in force that changes the Retreat Cost (imported Tools, Stadiums and Abilities do) is not read (Known gaps, counts item: `Count.retreat`, a departure in both directions for such a Pokémon) |
| `abilityByTool` | both | 3 | 'Pokémon that have an Ability' is `Filter.hasAbility`, which reads the printed Abilities and ignores an Ability a Tool gives in the model (Known gaps, filters: whether print counts a Tool's effect as the Pokémon's Ability is not settled); if it does, a Pokémon whose Ability comes from a Tool is not counted where print counts it, and an attacker with such an Ability is not prevented where print prevents its damage |
| `selfKOTiming` | both | 2 | the Knock Outs of an Ability's resolution are checked after each step (`TRun`): when the step before 'this Pokémon is Knocked Out' Knocks Out an opponent's Pokémon and so gives the player their last Prize card, the player wins before the self-Knock-Out step, where a check after the whole Ability would give both players their last Prize card at once, a tiebreaker (Known gaps, self-Knock-Out Abilities: timing) |
| `koBetweenSteps` | both | 1 | a Trainer or Ability sentence written as several primitives gets a Knock Out check between them, and after a Knock Out later steps act on the replacement (Known gaps, TRun, M8a) |
| `poisonStrength` | both | 1 | a stronger Poison ('N damage counters instead of 1') is written as Poison plus poisonUp (N-1), which a later Poison resets and Croagunk's increase adds to (Known gaps, Special Conditions: a variant with a number has no constructor of its own) |

Stacking texts ("The effect of X doesn't stack", "You can't apply more than 1 … at a time") in static Abilities: 6, all refused. The model adds every static effect in force, so two Pokémon with the Ability give twice the amount, where the printed card gives it once: a different HP, damage or reduction, which changes outcomes in both directions (more HP lets a Pokémon survive what the printed card Knocks Out, and a larger bonus Knocks Out what the printed card leaves standing), so the term would not be an over-approximation and an "allows more" caveat would be false. Pokémon Tools and Stadiums in the pool print no stacking text (a player has one Stadium in play; one Tool per Pokémon).

- Bouffalant (svp-136): "As long as you have at least 1 other Bouffalant in play, all of your Basic Colorless Pokémon take 60 less damage from attacks from your opponent's Pokémon (after applying Weakness and Resistance). The effect of Curly Wall doesn't stack." Refused; without the stacking sentence the rest is refused too (cond).
